intervals.quote: The CLAS12 experiment at the Jefferson Laboratory has begun the physics data taking in February 2018

placements.locator: CLAS12 NIM A959 abstract; first physics data February 2018 per PoS(SPIN2018)041
placements.quote: The CEBAF Large Acceptance Spectrometer for operation at 12 GeV beam energy (CLAS12) in Hall B at Jefferson Laboratory is used to study electro-induced nuclear and hadronic reactions.

subsystems.quote: CLAS12 is based on a dual-magnet system with a superconducting torus magnet that provides a largely azimuthal field distribution that covers the forward polar angle range up to 35
subsystems.value: Superconducting torus magnet covering forward polar angles up to 35 degrees; solenoid magnet and detector covering 35 to 125 degrees

summary.plain: A large detector with two magnets that surrounds the target in Hall B and tracks almost every charged and neutral particle produced when the 12 GeV electron beam strikes a target.
summary.technical: CLAS12: superconducting torus (forward polar angles up to 35 degrees, drift chambers) plus a superconducting solenoid and vertex tracker (35 to 125 degrees); Cherenkov counters, time-of-flight scintillators and electromagnetic calorimeters for particle identification; momentum resolution 1% forward and 3% central.

technology.quote: CLAS12 is based on a dual-magnet system with a superconducting torus magnet that provides a largely azimuthal field distribution that covers the forward polar angle range up to 35
technology.value: Dual-magnet large-acceptance spectrometer: superconducting torus with drift chambers (forward) and solenoid with vertex tracker (central), plus Cherenkov counters, time-of-flight scintillators and electromagnetic calorimeters
